comment: How the PostgreSQL schema of the TypeScript server (testdata/pg-v0.22.0.json) maps to schema.sql. MAPPING.md explains it; mapping_test.go checks it against both. A column, constraint or index named as a plain string maps to that name (a constraint to that kind: primary key, unique, foreign key, or a CHECK of the same name); 'dropped' gives the reason; a check marked 'rewritten' is not compared by expression.

types.rule: microseconds since the Unix epoch, UTC: PostgreSQL's own resolution, so no value changes
0 or 1, with CHECK (c IN (0, 1)); sqlc maps the column to bool (sqlc.json)
JSON text, with CHECK (json_valid(c)); compared as text, not by value
a JSON array of strings, with CHECK (json_valid(c) AND json_type(c) = 'array'); `= ANY ($1)` becomes json_each or IN

defaults.rule: the database clock in microseconds, at millisecond resolution; varlatchd passes its own times

account.dropped: Better Auth's provider accounts (passwords, OAuth tokens). Varlatch signs people in with passkeys only and creates their users itself, so no row is ever written; the migration (step 7) checks the table is empty.

approval_intents_target_check.rewritten: jsonb_typeof(target) = 'object' as json_type(target) = 'object', behind json_valid (json_type fails on text that is not JSON).

event_order.note: The rowid. Assigned by SQLite, checked by the trigger audit_events_position.

audit_events_pkey.note: id stays unique; the primary key is event_order, the table's rowid.

audit_events_order_idx.note: event_order is the INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (the rowid): SQLite assigns max + 1.

audit_position_insert.note: PostgreSQL assigned the position from a counter row locked until commit. SQLite assigns max(event_order) + 1 (the rowid); the single writer runs one job at a time and commits batches whole, so positions are in commit order without gaps; audit_events_position refuses any insert that is not the next position.

audit_export_plans_md5_check.rewritten: PostgreSQL's regular expression (~) as GLOB patterns and a length check, which accept exactly the same strings (mapping_test.go compares them on generated input).

audit_export_plans_sha256_check.rewritten: PostgreSQL's regular expression (~) as GLOB patterns and a length check, which accept exactly the same strings (mapping_test.go compares them on generated input).

audit_position.dropped: PostgreSQL's commit-order counter, a row locked until commit. In SQLite event_order is the rowid of audit_events and the single writer orders commits; the highest position is max(event_order) (query.LastAuditPosition).

device_sign_ins_user_code_check.rewritten: PostgreSQL's regular expression (~) as GLOB patterns and a length check, which accept exactly the same strings (mapping_test.go compares them on generated input).

exposure_backfill_singleton_check.rewritten: CHECK (singleton) on a boolean as singleton = 1 on its INTEGER.

id.note: PostgreSQL's default took 26 hex digits of an md5 of random() and the clock; SQLite takes 13 random bytes in hex. varlatchd names registrations itself.

github_app_registrations_account_login_c.rewritten: PostgreSQL's regular expression (~) as GLOB patterns and a length check, which accept exactly the same strings (mapping_test.go compares them on generated input).

github_app_registrations_pending_once.note: IS DISTINCT FROM is IS NOT. jsonb compared by value, SQLite JSON text by its text: rewriting the pending key in another spelling is refused too.

installation_singleton.rewritten: LIKE 'inst_%' (where _ is any one character) as GLOB 'inst?*'; GLOB is case-sensitive like PostgreSQL's LIKE.

passkey_credentialID_idx.dropped: Redundant: the unique index passkey_credential_id_unique (migration 0039) covers the same column.

passkey_counter_forward.note: The function's condition is the trigger's WHEN clause; RAISE(ABORT) is SQLite's constraint error (SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_TRIGGER), a job's own error in lib/storage.

passkey.note: Better Auth's table, in its adapter's shape; varlatchd owns it now, so it takes a snake_case name, and so do its columns. Row ids are kept. A passkey's user_id is its WebAuthn user handle.

passkey_quarantine.note: Copies passkey's columns, so they take the same snake_case names.

security_control_counters_bucket_hour_ch.rewritten: date_trunc('hour', bucket_hour, 'UTC') = bucket_hour as bucket_hour % 3600000000 = 0 on microseconds since the epoch.

security_control_counters_operation_chec.rewritten: PostgreSQL's regular expression (~) as GLOB patterns and a length check, which accept exactly the same strings (mapping_test.go compares them on generated input).

security_controls_config_check.rewritten: jsonb_typeof(x) = 'number' as json_type(...) IN ('integer', 'real'), (config ->> k)::numeric as json_extract(config, '$.k'), behind json_valid.

token.note: Better Auth stored the session token itself; varlatchd stores its hash (step 3.4). Nothing is copied: sessions end at the migration.

session_end_revokes_browser_credentials.note: A row trigger (SQLite has no statement triggers) on auth_sessions: one statement deleting several sessions writes their events session by session, each session's in credential id order, where PostgreSQL wrote all of them in credential id order. No locks: the single writer holds the only write transaction.

session.note: Better Auth's table, in its adapter's shape; varlatchd owns it now, so it takes a snake_case name, and so do its columns. Row ids are kept. No session is copied by the migration: every browser session ends (ADR-0059 Decision 9).

sync_cursor_singleton_check.rewritten: CHECK (singleton) on a boolean as singleton = 1 on its INTEGER.

user.note: Better Auth's table, in its adapter's shape; varlatchd owns it now, so it takes a snake_case name, and so do its columns. Row ids are kept.

varlatch_migrations.dropped: The PostgreSQL migration runner's bookkeeping. The SQLite schema is created whole, not replayed, and records its version in schema_version.

verification.dropped: Better Auth's short-lived ceremony challenges (minutes). varlatchd keeps its own ceremony challenges (step 3.4); no row needs to survive a migration, which ends every browser session anyway.

assign_audit_position.note: Replaced: the rowid assigns the position, the trigger checks it.

new_audit_event_id.note: Inlined in the trigger: 'evt_' and 26 base32 characters from random().

exposure_backfill.note: One row, finished at once: a new database has no audit history to backfill (migration 0036).

audit_position.dropped: The table is dropped; the position is max(event_order).

triggers.audit_events_no_update: Audit events are append-only. PostgreSQL withheld UPDATE and DELETE on audit_events from the runtime role (migration 0003); SQLite has no roles.
